column4: Catalogue tension from the manufacturer's product page (Wayback capture of 2019-12-13, thomastik-infeld.com/en/products/orchestral-strings/double-bass/spirocore-orchestra, MEDIUM row of the 110.0 cm table): E 34.0, A 34.0, D 32.0, G 30.0 kg; converted with 9.80665 m/s^2, reading kg as kilogram-force

column4: Line mass derived from published inputs, not weighed: mu = T / (2 L f)^2 (Mersenne) with T from the tension observation, L = 1.100 m and f the equal-tempered open-string frequency (E1 41.2034, A1 55.0000, D2 73.4162, G2 97.9989 Hz at A4 = 440 Hz)
column5: Cross-check on A1 against Zupet 2024 (University of Ljubljana MSc, p. 24, as quoted by the lead in mail 15933; thesis not opened by PlumCanyon): Spirocore Medium 4/4 A, L 1100 mm, f0 55.0 Hz, mu 22.8 g/m, T 333.5 N

column4: No unit is printed. Read as inches: it is the only unit for which mu / (pi d^2 / 4) stays below steel's 7850 kg/m^3 for all four strings; read as millimetres it would exceed it by about six orders of magnitude
column5: The row is Spirocore Mittel of unstated size, not the 4/4 Orchestra set that gives the tension. On this route the diameter enters only through the computed air drag

column3: The Spirocore spiral rope core (the page says only 'Spiral core'); bending stiffness is unpublished
column4: Bounds, not measurements. Upper: the load-bearing core as a solid steel rod, EI = E pi d_c^4 / 64 with E = 200 GPa; A string d_c = 0.75 mm (Zupet 2024 via the lead, mail 15933); the E, D and G cores scaled as d_c = 0.75 mm x sqrt(T / T_A) (equal core stress, an assumption). Lower: the same core as a close-packed 1 x 7 bundle of free wires of diameter d_c / 3 with no friction between wires, EI = 7/81 of the upper
column5: The wire count 7 and the core scaling are assumptions of this card; the winding adds no stiffness in either bound. The effect of the unknown is measured by rendering both
